trigger: coordinator-measured outage: query_l_space_concept and search_l_space both returned 'L-Space release is unavailable: /home/emsenn/info/dist/vault/manifest.json'

phase1Repair.rootCause: src/release-observation.mjs's DEFAULT_L_SPACE_RELEASE_ROOT used to be resolve("dist/vault"), resolved against process.cwd(). When the MCP launcher did not honor .mcp.json's configured cwd for the l-space server, that resolved to the repo root, which never had a dist/ directory — the exact path in the outage report.
phase1Repair.priorFix: Already committed today by an earlier session at 657694e893003704a31fd34584ed717fa6784362 ('l-space: resolve release root relative to module dir, not cwd'): DEFAULT_L_SPACE_RELEASE_ROOT is now resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "dist", "vault") — cwd-independent. This session verified the fix is correct and not a hand-authored workaround.
phase1Repair.secondaryDefect: The dist/vault directory on disk at session start was stale relative to the current build pipeline: it carried manifest.json and index.json but no graph.json, no victor-release.json, no views/, and its manifest's graph.schemaVersion was the literal string 'n/a' — a value the current scripts/build-cloud-release.mjs never emits (it always writes 'l-space-release-graph/v1'). This made query_l_space_concept fail even after the cwd fix, because it needs graph.json via src/release-graph-reader.mjs.
phase1Repair.generator: scripts/build-cloud-release.mjs (invoked as `npm run build:cloud`, which runs `build:engine` then this script) is the sole, real generator of dist/vault/*.json in the tree — confirmed by grep across the repo for any other writer of vault/manifest.json or vault/index.json. Never hand-authored; regenerated by running the canonical script.
phase1Repair.distIsBuildOutput: lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/science-services-section/sites/l-space.561.group/.gitignore contains `dist/` — dist/vault is confirmed gitignored build product, regenerated on demand, never committed. It is not a missing release artifact needing a documented home.
phase1Repair.fixApplied: Ran `npm run build:cloud` fresh in the site directory. Produced a complete, internally consistent release: manifest.json schemaVersion l-space-release-graph/v1 for graph, graph.json (51MB), index.json (20MB), victor-release.json (12MB), views/, public/. phase2Elevation.standardAssessed: one call answering a concept query with: the ruled/glossary definition (with provenance), the top theory carriers ranked by load-bearingness, the Lean formalization path if Obsmetrologia carries one, and the live realizations (packages/sections implementing it).
phase2Elevation.dataModelGapFound: GEODE's query_l_space_concept (apps/geode/src/concept-index.mjs projectConcept/concept()) answers from the 'declares-keyword' declared-relation ledger only. Its `known` field is false for a concept that is fully ruled as a house glossary term but is not itself declared as a compound-term keyword by another document — demonstrated live: querying 'endeavor' returned known:false, definedBy:[], even though services/information-science-services-section/.../glossary/terms/endeavor.md and a second philosophy-section definition both rule it. Raw grep of the vault or the old broken MCP would give an agent no way to tell 'ruled but not keyword-declared' from 'not in the corpus at all'.

implemented.what: Added glossaryProvenanceOf(name) to src/release-observation.mjs: a plain path check against the house glossary convention (content/text/glossary/terms/<name>.md, matching CLAUDE.md's own stated convention), returning {ruled, statement, room, additionalDefinitions}. Wired into scripts/serve-mcp.mjs's query_l_space_concept handler so every concept reading now carries a provenance field alongside GEODE's declared-relation reading.
implemented.why: This is the highest-value, cleanly-achievable slice of the standard achievable in one pass: it closes exactly the false-negative demonstrated above, using data already loaded by the release snapshot (no new file reads, no schema change to GEODE itself, so no risk to GEODE's other consumers).
implemented.verified: query_l_space_concept({name: 'endeavor'}) now returns known:false (GEODE's narrower keyword-declaration signal, left untouched) alongside provenance.ruled:true with both definitions' room paths (services/information-science-services-section/... and services/philosophy-services-section/...). Tests added to test/release-observation.test.mjs (3 new cases); full suite still 86/86 passing.

meetGapRoadmap.incumbent: raw markdown-vault grep / ad hoc session-level corpus grepping — the documented months-long substitute while L-Space MCP was dead
meetGapRoadmap.differentiatorAlreadyHeld: content-addressed immutable release (sha256 room keys, one signed manifest), a real declared-relation graph (not text match), bounded SPARQL BGP over EAVT, and now plain glossary-provenance — none of which raw grep can produce

gaps.item: top theory carriers ranked by load-bearingness, not raw match count
gaps.mechanism: query_l_space_fae_entity({term: <glossary room id>, direction: 'incoming'}) already exposes FAE door in-degree for a room — the count of other corpus documents linking to a concept's glossary term is a real load-bearingness signal (as opposed to search's keyword-weight score field, which only measures title/path text match). Next step: have query_l_space_concept call faeEntity on the ruled room (when provenance.ruled) and surface incoming-door count as a ranking signal on definedBy/keywordBacklinks, sorted descending.
gaps.risk: FAE entity queries are per-room and were not load-tested at concept-query time across the whole 10562-room corpus in this pass; needs a latency check before wiring into the hot path.

gaps.mechanism: The real, non-legacy Obsmetrologia proof root is at science-services-section/services/information-science-services-section/services/math-services-section/services/obsmetrological-services-section/lib/obsmetrologia/Obsmetrologia.lean, with 936 .lean files under Obsmetrologia/ organized by theorem-locus (Settlement.lean, Closure.lean, Cohomology.lean, Site.lean, ...) per org-layering.md's rule 2. No mapping from a glossary concept name to a Lean module path exists anywhere in the pipeline today — neither in glossary frontmatter nor in GEODE. Next step is a design choice, not free-hand code: either (a) a frontmatter field on ruled glossary terms naming their Lean module, authored by hand where a real formalization exists, or (b) a heuristic filename-index over the 936 files, cached once, matched against the concept name and its aliases. (a) is more honest (states only real formalizations); (b) covers more concepts but risks false positives from name coincidence.
gaps.risk: Guessing a Lean path from name-matching alone would misattribute a formalization that does not actually correspond to the glossary concept — a correctness risk, not just an engineering one.

gaps.status: not implemented this pass; mechanism spiked
gaps.mechanism: mcp__jsnode-server__jsnode_search (ranked capability-owner search over the whole package graph) was tested live in this session: query 'endeavor' correctly returned zero matches (a plain-English concept with no package), while query 'settlement' returned a very large ranked result set (~8500 lines), confirming the tool is a real, working live-realization index for engineering-shaped concepts. It is not yet wired into query_l_space_concept.
gaps.risk: jsnode_search's raw output is far too large to embed directly in a concept card (8500+ lines for one query); it needs a bounded/ranked adapter (top-N by the tool's own name>keyword>description ranking) before it can be surfaced safely inside an MCP tool response.
